intent_en: To explain the economic mechanism behind yield curve inversion, illustrating how gloomy outlooks drive investors to buy long-term bonds and lower long-term interest rates.
previous_intent: To explain the economic mechanism behind yield curve inversion, illustrating how a gloomy outlook leads investors to buy long-term bonds and lower long-term interest rates.
narration_support: When the outlook is gloomy, investors are more likely to buy safe assets, like long -term bonds, pushing their price up so the interest rate for holding them falls.
chart_support: Line chart titled 'Yield curve' plotting 'Interest rate' against 'Time' (3m to 10y), displaying the relationship between bond maturity and interest rates.
evidence_note: The narration explains the causal mechanism (investor behavior lowering rates), while the chart visualizes the yield curve structure (Interest rate vs Time) that is being analyzed. The chart shows a normal upward-sloping curve, establishing the baseline variables for the explanation of inversion.
